format_coverage: Microsoft does not publish the item types used on a given exam ("To protect exam security and the value of our certifications, we don't identify specific exam formats or question types before the exam"). What it does publish is the sample list demoed in its exam sandbox — multiple choice, drag and drop, hot area, build list, active screen and case studies (labs do not apply to Fundamentals exams) — plus confirmation that "problem-solution question sets" exist, where one scenario is restated with a different proposed solution and answered Yes or No. This mock supports three formats and approximates as follows. Multiple choice maps exactly to single_choice, and the problem-solution shape is authored as a two-option single_choice (the individual item maps; the sibling relationship within a series does not). Multi-select multiple choice maps to multiple_response. Drag and drop is approximated by scenario_matching. Hot area (a grid of statements each answered independently) is approximated by multiple_response "select every true statement", which loses the per-statement No branch. Build list (place steps in order) is approximated by single_choice over permutations of the same steps. Active screen (configure a control in a rendered interface) and case studies (several dependent items under one shared scenario) are not represented at all; their underlying concepts are authored as standalone items. Two scoring divergences are disclosed alongside: the real exam awards partial credit on multi-part items (one point per correctly answered component) where this mock's multiple_response is all-or-nothing, and the real exam reports a scaled 1-1000 score with 700 to pass — which Microsoft states "may not equal 70% of the points" — where this mock reports percent correct against a 70% bar.
